# Joel Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 333v–334r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOL_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Sound the alarm in Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet on God's holy mountain! Let everyone in the land tremble with fear, for the day of the LORD is coming — it is almost here!

**2** It is a day of darkness and gloom, a day of thick clouds and deep blackness. Like dawn spreading across the mountains, a great and mighty army appears — an army unlike anything before in all of history, and nothing like it will ever be seen again.

**3** Fire goes ahead of them and flames follow behind. Before them the land is as beautiful as the Garden of Eden; behind them it is a barren wasteland. Nothing escapes.

**4** They look like horses; they charge like warhorses. **5** Listen to them as they leap along the mountaintops — it sounds like the rumble of chariots, like the roar of fire sweeping across a field, like a mighty army moving into position for battle.

**6** Terror grips the people as they approach; every face turns pale. **7** They charge like warriors. They scale walls like soldiers. They march in formation, never breaking ranks. **8** They never crowd each other; each one marches straight ahead. They plunge through defenses without breaking stride. **9** They swarm over the city walls. They invade the houses. They climb in through the windows like thieves.

**10** The earth shakes as they advance. The sky trembles. The sun and moon go dark, and the stars no longer shine. **11** The LORD thunders at the head of his army. His forces are beyond counting. How powerful are those who obey his commands! The day of the LORD is truly awesome and terrifying. Who can survive it?

**12** "But even now," declares the LORD, "come back to me with all your heart — with fasting, weeping, and mourning." **13** Don't tear your clothing in grief — tear your hearts instead. Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to get angry, and filled with unfailing love. He is eager to relent and not punish. **14** Who knows? Perhaps he will give you a reprieve, sending you a blessing instead of a curse. Perhaps you will be able to offer grain and wine to the LORD your God as before.

**15** Blow the trumpet in Jerusalem! Announce a time of fasting; call the people together for a solemn meeting. **16** Gather everyone — the elders, the children, even the nursing babies. Call the bridegroom from his room and the bride from her honeymoon.

**17** Let the priests, who minister to the LORD, weep between the Temple entrance and the altar. Let them pray, "Spare your people, LORD! Don't let your special possession become an object of mockery. Don't let them become a joke for the other nations. Don't give them reason to say, 'Where is the God of Israel?'"

**18** Then the LORD burned with zeal for his land and took pity on his people. **19** The LORD replied, "Look! I am sending you grain and new wine and olive oil — enough to satisfy you fully. And I will no longer make you an object of mockery among the nations."

**20** "I will drive away the army from the north and push it into a dry and barren land. Those in front will be driven into the Dead Sea, and those behind into the Mediterranean. The stench of the dead will rise across the land." Truly the LORD has done great things!

**21** Don't be afraid, my people! Be glad now and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things. **22** Don't be afraid, you animals of the field! The wilderness pastures will soon be green. The trees will bear fruit again. Fig trees and grapevines will be loaded with crops.

**23** Rejoice, people of Jerusalem! Rejoice in the LORD your God! For the rain he sends demonstrates his faithfulness. Once more the autumn rains will come, as well as the spring rains, as before.

**24** The threshing floors will again be piled high with grain, and the presses will overflow with new wine and olive oil. **25** "I will give you back what you lost to the swarming locusts, the hopping locusts, the stripping locusts, and the cutting locusts — my great army that I sent against you."

**26** "Once again you will have all the food you want, and you will praise the LORD your God, who does these miracles for you. Never again will my people be disgraced. **27** Then you will know that I am among my people Israel, that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other. Never again will my people be disgraced."

**28** "After all of this, I will pour out my Spirit on everyone. Your sons and daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions. **29** In those days I will pour out my Spirit even on servants — men and women alike."

**30** "I will cause wonders in the heavens and on the earth — blood and fire and billowing smoke. **31** The sun will become dark, and the moon will turn blood red before the great and terrible day of the LORD arrives. **32** But everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved. There will be people who escape on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, just as the LORD has said. They will be among the survivors whom the LORD has called."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The locust army (vv.1-11):** Joel's description of the locust plague morphs into an apocalyptic army — soldiers who scale walls, enter windows, and darken the sky. The description deliberately keeps the reader unsure: are these insects or soldiers? Joel's answer seems to be "yes." The locust plague is a real event that functions as a preview of the day of the LORD.

**"Rend your hearts, not your garments" (v.13):** One of the most powerful prophetic calls in the Bible. External religion — tearing clothes, fasting, weeping — means nothing without internal transformation. The same Exodus 34:6 creed that Joel quotes here (gracious, merciful, slow to anger) is also quoted by Jonah, but to opposite effect: Jonah resents God's mercy; Joel relies on it.

**The Spirit on all flesh (vv.28-29):** The most radical promise in the book. In the old system, God's Spirit rested on selected individuals — prophets, kings, judges. Joel envisions a complete democratization: everyone receives the Spirit — old and young, men and women, even servants. Peter saw this fulfilled at Pentecost (Acts 2).

*— PNEUMA*
